extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in comedy, pop culture, and the history of celebrity roasts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria for what a celebrity roast is and how it works in practice — its tone, performers, medium constraints, purpose (fundraising/PR), and the roastee's required disposition. Focused on televised and private/club roasts (Friars Club, Dean Martin, Comedy Central).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insulting guests of honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Insulting guests of honor was originally a way to raise money for veterans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The roast tradition is 'steeped in insults and offensive humor' and centers on making the guest the butt of jokes as the primary mode of tribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor via verbal disembowelment
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature colleagues coming together to 'honor' a special guest by means of verbal disembowelment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ceremony of the roast is framed as an honor even though the method is harsh, teasing, and brutal in tone; this paradox is central to the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requires thick skin
rubrics_metrics.description: It takes thick skin to endure these events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because roasts use insults and offensive humor (and may include heavy booing or harsh barbs), the roastee must be prepared to shrug off personal attacks or risk a 'nightmarish' experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional/mental preparedness of the roastee
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you’re set mentally and emotionally, it could have a nightmarish quality to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (Chevy Chase, William Shatner) show that being unprepared—friends absent, unexpected cruelty—can make roasts psychologically damaging rather than celebratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private club origins and audience restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: These events were private and limited to members and guests only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early Friars Club roasts were inside gatherings not intended for primetime; their private nature allowed much dirtier, more authentic material that wouldn't suit broadcast standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profanity and medium constraints (network vs cable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some roast formats refrained from being profane on network television, while cable could capture the true Friars sensibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dean Martin's NBC roasts 'refrained from being profane' to fit network standards; Comedy Central and later cable/streaming allowed the dirtier, more authentic version of roasts (and thus different comedic choices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Production/technical effects on authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of the roasts were taped in two places, with footage being spliced together. Some jokes might be delivered to an empty room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Television production techniques (taping at multiple locations, editing) can reduce spontaneity and audience reaction, affecting the perceived authenticity and punch of jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the roastmaster and skilled insult comedians
rubrics_metrics.description: Having a roastmaster and accomplished insult comics is central — e.g., Don Rickles as an 'insult legend' and Jeff Ross having 'perfected the art of the insult.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A skilled roastmaster (or comics with a talent for barbs) structures the show, escalates jokes, and gives the roast its comedic edge; star performers can define the event's tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising / charitable purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Dinners were organized to help raise money for veterans; some roasted performers opted to donate proceeds to charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roasts historically served philanthropic goals (WWI veterans fundraising) and modern roastees sometimes donate proceeds, framing the event as socially beneficial despite harsh humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience composition and presence of friends
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of friends/peers matters to the roastee's experience (e.g., Chevy Chase was 'stunned...then angry...then devastated' when friends didn't show).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supportive audience context (peers, colleagues) helps signal the performative/affectionate intent of insults; an unsupportive audience amplifies harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential PR and career effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Roasts can wind up having a net positive effect — e.g., Charlie Sheen's 2011 roast is credited with helping rejuvenate his image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond momentary humiliation, a roast can be leveraged for publicity or image rehabilitation when managed and received well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation and archival value
rubrics_metrics.description: The Friars Club's past is being preserved (e.g., SiriusXM announced a channel devoted to audio of the private roasts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archiving roasts preserves comedic history and can make private performances available to wider audiences, affecting cultural legacy.
